meta.title: CAD Guardian Paid Engagement Workflow Corpus
meta.positioning: You have drawings due. We keep them moving.
meta.governance: Public prices and claims must remain synchronized with the approved commercial catalog, Stripe, proposal templates and CRM. Client names and confidential evidence require written approval.

commercialLadder.name: Paid Diagnostic
commercialLadder.purpose: Convert an urgent or ambiguous operating problem into a bounded decision, evidence map, risk register and prioritized next move.
commercialLadder.payment: Stripe Checkout or Payment Link; 100% before kickoff after scope acceptance.
commercialLadder.gate: One system, package class or contributor-to-issued-output workflow.

commercialLadder.name: System Blueprint
commercialLadder.purpose: Define the future-state workflow, technical architecture, controls, backlog, acceptance criteria and implementation economics.
commercialLadder.payment: Stripe invoice; 50% kickoff / 50% delivery, or 100% prepaid for qualified buyers.
commercialLadder.gate: Diagnostic evidence accepted; sponsor and system owner available.

commercialLadder.name: Production-Shaped Prototype
commercialLadder.purpose: Prove the highest-risk automation or integration path against representative files and real operating constraints.
commercialLadder.payment: Milestone invoice; 50% kickoff / 30% working proof / 20% acceptance.
commercialLadder.gate: Representative data, test environment and acceptance owner confirmed.

commercialLadder.name: Drawing / Document Automation Slice
commercialLadder.purpose: Automate one bounded drawing, model, BOM, transmittal or document-production workflow.
commercialLadder.payment: Milestone invoice tied to evidence, UAT and deployment gates.
commercialLadder.gate: One defined output family with measurable baseline and controlled exceptions.

commercialLadder.name: Implementation Build Slice
commercialLadder.purpose: Deploy a governed production capability with integration, telemetry, documentation, rollback and handoff.
commercialLadder.payment: 30% kickoff / 30% production-shaped build / 25% UAT / 15% release and handoff.
commercialLadder.gate: Named executive sponsor, technical owner, access path and change-control authority.

commercialLadder.name: Care & Change — Foundation
commercialLadder.purpose: Controlled maintenance, backlog triage, minor enhancements and operating review for one production capability.
commercialLadder.payment: Stripe subscription or recurring invoice, billed in advance.
commercialLadder.gate: Stable deployed boundary and named owner.

commercialLadder.name: Care & Change — Growth / Critical
commercialLadder.purpose: Priority engineering capacity, release support, workflow expansion, incident response and executive operating review.
commercialLadder.payment: Stripe subscription or recurring invoice, billed in advance with overage/change-order rules.
commercialLadder.gate: Agreed service envelope, response targets and capacity reservation.

workflows.name: Drawing Deadline Rescue
workflows.trigger: A drawing or model package is behind, inconsistent, failing review or due within days and internal leadership is spending expensive time correcting production defects.
workflows.fear: Missed issue date, client embarrassment, principal rework, uncontrolled outsourcing, incomplete native files and an unreliable package that cannot be defended.
workflows.outcome: A controlled recovery plan, explicit source hierarchy, visible unknowns, prioritized production queue and independently checked issue package.
scope: One named project and issue milestone
Native-file audit and PDF visual QA
Issue log, assumptions and handoff record
deliverables: Corrected native files and issued PDFs where authorized
discovery: What is due, to whom and at what exact time?
Which sheets or models are blocking issue?
What is the trusted prior package or office standard?
Who can answer design questions and accept exceptions?
Which source files, fonts, plot styles, links and references are available?
What work is explicitly not authorized?
disqualify: No access to source files or approver
workflows.roi: Compare avoided principal correction hours, delay exposure, remobilization and client-risk cost against fixed rescue fee. Do not promise unverified savings.

objections.a: More hands amplify ambiguity when standards, dependencies and review state are not controlled. Rescue starts by making authority and critical path explicit.
A date commitment follows source preflight, scope freeze and reviewer availability. Unknown design decisions remain visible rather than fabricated.

workflows.talkTrack: The product is not emergency labor. It is controlled recovery: establish what is true, isolate what blocks issue, move the package, and leave a defensible record.

workflows.name: Drawing Package & Standards Reliability Diagnostic
workflows.trigger: Packages repeatedly require principal correction, outside contributors return inconsistent files, or standards exist but do not survive handoff.
workflows.fear: The firm cannot scale delivery without quality erosion, key-person dependence and repeated rework.
workflows.outcome: A decision-ready map of the contributor-to-issued-output system, its governing standards, failure modes and first controlled improvement.
scope: One package class or contributor-to-issued-output workflow
Template, font, CTB/STB, Xref and dependency inventory
discovery: Where does a package change hands?
Who owns standards versus who approves issue?
How are exceptions and revisions recorded?
What percentage of senior time is consumed correcting output?
qualify: Sponsor can provide two to five representative packages
Leadership wants a decision rather than free advice
disqualify: No authority to inspect examples or interview owners
workflows.roi: Baseline senior correction hours, rejected submissions, cycle delay and contributor ramp time. Build an evidence-backed range, not a generic productivity claim.

objections.q: We already have a CAD manual.
objections.a: A manual is one control. The diagnostic tests whether authority, dependencies, examples, review states and exceptions actually produce reliable issued output.
The diagnostic prevents automating the wrong behavior and defines the bounded change with the highest operational return.

workflows.talkTrack: When the principal is the final error-correction system, the firm does not have a scalable production system. We expose where trust breaks and define the smallest corrective move.

workflows.name: CAD/BIM Standards Handoff System
workflows.trigger: Internal and external contributors interpret standards differently, onboarding is oral and review feedback repeats across projects.
workflows.fear: Growth increases correction cost, outsourcing becomes a management burden and standards depend on one person’s memory.
workflows.outcome: A usable operating system that converts standards into role-specific intake, production, review, exception and acceptance controls.
scope: Layer, family, view, sheet and plotting controls
exclusions: Writing an entire office standard from nothing
discovery: Which errors recur by contributor type?
What must be true before work begins?
Where are standards stored and who can supersede them?
What does an accepted native file look like?
disqualify: Buyer wants surveillance rather than workflow control
workflows.roi: Measure contributor ramp time, first-pass acceptance, review rounds and senior correction hours before and after the pilot.

objections.q: Our people will not follow another process.
objections.a: The system is built around the actual handoff and reduces ambiguity at the moment work begins; it is not another generic manual.

workflows.talkTrack: Standards become valuable only when a contributor can start correctly, self-check, surface an exception and know what acceptance means.

workflows.name: AutoCAD Batch Production Automation
workflows.trigger: Teams repeat plotting, attribute updates, layer cleanup, title-block edits, file conversion, standards checks or drawing generation across many DWGs.
workflows.fear: Manual volume creates inconsistent output, deadline pressure, overtime and silent errors that appear only at issue.
workflows.outcome: A bounded, auditable batch workflow that turns representative input into repeatable output with logs, exceptions and rollback.
scope: AutoCAD .NET, AutoLISP, Core Console or approved execution path
disqualify: Buyer expects automation to infer design intent
workflows.roi: Volume × manual minutes × loaded rate, adjusted for exception handling, avoided rework and release risk. Validate with timed sample runs.

objections.q: We can write a quick script internally.
objections.a: A production tool includes version control, backups, logs, failure isolation, acceptance tests, deployment and an owner—not only a macro that works on one machine.

workflows.talkTrack: We automate the boring path and make the exceptional path visible. The goal is repeatability, not hidden magic.

workflows.name: Revit Model & Sheet Stabilization
workflows.trigger: A model has unstable views, inconsistent sheets, duplicated content, broken links, warnings, unreliable plotting or unclear ownership near a deliverable.
workflows.fear: Late model failure, corrupted deliverables, untraceable changes and senior staff spending the deadline repairing production mechanics.
workflows.outcome: A bounded stabilization plan and corrected deliverable path that preserves evidence, isolates uncertainty and restores issue control.
scope: Native reopen test and PDF QA
discovery: What exact model and issue set governs?
Which warnings are accepted versus blocking?
What changed since the last trusted issue?
Which views or sheets are known unreliable?
disqualify: Buyer requests silent alteration of design
workflows.roi: Quantify avoided deadline rework, senior correction hours and issue-delay exposure. Do not equate warning count alone with business value.

objections.a: Warnings are classified by consequence. The engagement removes or documents what affects the defined deliverable rather than chasing a cosmetic zero.

workflows.talkTrack: We separate model health from design authority, stabilize the deliverable boundary and leave the team with an explicit record of what remains.

workflows.name: LiDAR / Point Cloud to Existing Conditions
workflows.trigger: A renovation or documentation project has scan data, field photos and legacy drawings but no reliable existing-condition plan/model package.
workflows.fear: False precision, invented geometry, wasted site visits and downstream design built on misunderstood scan evidence.
workflows.outcome: A confidence-labeled existing-condition package that distinguishes observed geometry, inferred relationships and unresolved conditions.
scope: Native file and PDF package QA
discovery: What scanner and export produced the data?
What coordinate system and units govern?
Which levels and areas are sufficiently covered?
qualify: Evidence gaps may be shown openly
disqualify: Buyer demands complete geometry despite missing evidence
Data cannot be opened or located
workflows.roi: Compare reduced field revisits, avoided remodel rework and faster existing-condition production against engagement cost, while preserving uncertainty.

objections.q: Why not let AI generate the floor plan?
objections.a: Existing conditions require evidence lineage and confidence. Automation may accelerate extraction, but unsupported geometry remains unsupported.

workflows.talkTrack: The deliverable is not a confident-looking model. It is a usable model whose confidence is explicit enough for the next professional decision.

workflows.name: Drawing & Model QA Automation
workflows.trigger: Reviewers repeatedly check the same naming, layer, family, sheet, title-block, reference, metadata or publication rules by eye.
workflows.fear: Critical checks are skipped under pressure, QA quality depends on reviewer memory and defects are discovered after issue.
workflows.outcome: A governed validation layer that identifies deterministic defects, records evidence and routes judgment-based exceptions to people.
workflows.roi: Measure review minutes per package, escape defects and recheck cycles. Value deterministic checks while retaining human judgment.

objections.q: Will this replace our QA reviewers?
objections.a: No. It removes repeatable inspection burden and gives reviewers more time for coordination, intent and professional judgment.

workflows.talkTrack: Machines should enforce explicit rules. People should decide exceptions and design consequences.

workflows.name: Quote/RFQ Workflow Diagnostic
workflows.trigger: Quote requests move through email and spreadsheets, engineering re-enters information, configuration rules are unclear or proposal documents are slow and inconsistent.
workflows.fear: Long quote cycle, margin leakage, wrong configuration, missed follow-up and a commercial promise engineering cannot reliably fulfill.
workflows.outcome: A bounded current-state map, economic baseline and first automation decision across intake, configuration, engineering, pricing, approval and document output.
discovery: Which outputs are generated and from what source?
disqualify: Buyer wants a generic CRM implementation
workflows.roi: Model quote volume, elapsed time, touch time, re-entry, correction, conversion and margin-risk ranges using buyer evidence.

objections.a: The diagnostic follows the engineering decision and document path, including the work that happens outside the CRM.

workflows.talkTrack: The target is not another form. It is a controlled path from commercial request to an engineering-feasible, priced and approved output.

workflows.name: Quote Automation Prototype
workflows.trigger: A diagnostic has identified one high-value configuration or document-generation path that can be proved without rebuilding the entire commercial stack.
workflows.fear: A large implementation begins before data, rules, integration and adoption risks are understood.
workflows.outcome: A production-shaped proof that demonstrates data flow, decision logic, exception handling and output generation on representative cases.
discovery: Which uncertainty must the prototype retire?
What is the smallest useful end-to-end case?
What systems can be read safely?
What must be logged for trust?
disqualify: Buyer wants production rollout disguised as prototype
workflows.roi: Value the retired implementation risk, demonstrated cycle reduction and validated scope—not speculative enterprise-wide savings.

objections.q: Why not build the whole system?
objections.a: The prototype proves the riskiest vertical slice before capital and organizational commitment expand.

workflows.talkTrack: We prove one complete path with real constraints, then let evidence—not enthusiasm—govern the build decision.

workflows.name: Inventor, BOM & Document Automation
workflows.trigger: Engineers repeatedly update parameters, drawings, parts lists, BOM exports, PDFs or release documents across configurable products.
workflows.fear: Drawing/BOM disagreement, manual release errors, outdated VBA, dependence on one expert and delayed production handoff.
workflows.outcome: One controlled model-to-document workflow with explicit parameters, validation, generated outputs and release evidence.
discovery: Which parameters drive geometry and documents?
disqualify: Rules live only in undocumented individual judgment
workflows.roi: Measure engineering touch time, output count, change propagation, correction cycles and release delay on representative configurations.

objections.a: iLogic may remain part of the solution. The engagement addresses governance, testability, deployment, logging and cross-document reliability around it.

workflows.talkTrack: The objective is not to generate more files faster. It is to keep model, BOM, drawing and release output synchronized under controlled change.

workflows.name: Vault / PDM Release Workflow Stabilization
workflows.trigger: Files, revisions, lifecycle states, properties, jobs or published outputs do not move reliably through Vault/PDM and teams maintain parallel truth outside the system.
workflows.fear: Wrong revision reaches manufacturing, release ownership is unclear, job processors fail silently and engineering data cannot be trusted.
workflows.outcome: A bounded, observable release path with explicit state ownership, property mapping, job behavior, exception handling and recovery.
scope: One release workflow or file family
discovery: Who can promote, reject or roll back?
What jobs run and where do failures surface?
How is a bad release recovered?
disqualify: Buyer expects connector to solve governance disputes
workflows.roi: Quantify release delay, manual publishing, revision escapes, retry burden and downstream disruption using actual incidents.

objections.a: The platform provides capabilities; reliable operation still depends on lifecycle design, property ownership, jobs, exceptions and support controls.

workflows.talkTrack: A release system is trustworthy when state, data, output, failure and recovery are all visible—not merely when files are checked in.

workflows.name: Legacy CAD Utility Modernization
workflows.trigger: A critical AutoLISP, VBA, macro, add-in or desktop utility is fragile, undocumented, tied to an old platform or maintained by one person.
workflows.fear: A version upgrade breaks a trusted workflow, the original developer is unavailable and a rewrite changes business behavior.
workflows.outcome: Preserved trusted behavior, exposed dependencies, regression evidence and a bounded modernization path without a big-bang rewrite.
scope: One utility or cohesive command set
One bounded migration or stabilization slice
exclusions: All internal tools at one fixed price
discovery: Who uses it and how often?
What data or files can be damaged?
disqualify: No one can define correct behavior
Buyer insists on full rewrite before discovery
workflows.roi: Compare outage/replacement exposure, manual fallback burden, upgrade delay and support cost against the bounded modernization investment.

objections.q: Why not rewrite it in the newest stack?
objections.a: First preserve and test the behavior the business trusts. Technology choice follows the operating contract, not fashion.

workflows.talkTrack: Modernization succeeds when trusted behavior survives and future change becomes safer—not when every line is replaced.

workflows.name: Engineering Systems Integration Build Slice
workflows.trigger: CAD/BIM/PDM output, ERP data, quote records, documents and approvals require repeated entry or reconciliation across systems.
workflows.fear: Conflicting records, brittle point integrations, invisible failures and a transformation program that expands before one path is reliable.
workflows.outcome: One production-grade integration slice with source ownership, contracts, observability, retries, reconciliation, security and rollback.
discovery: What happens when either system is unavailable?
disqualify: Buyer asks for broad integration platform before first use case
workflows.roi: Measure re-entry touch time, data defects, elapsed handoff, exception recovery and business delay on the selected event.

objections.a: The first objective is one observable, recoverable business event. A portfolio can grow from evidence after that path is stable.

workflows.talkTrack: Integration is complete only when ownership, failure, reconciliation and recovery are as explicit as the happy-path API call.

workflows.name: Care & Change Engineering Retainer
workflows.trigger: A deployed workflow, automation or delivery system now needs controlled maintenance, enhancement, release support and accountable ownership.
workflows.fear: The new capability becomes another orphaned tool, changes bypass testing and urgent support depends on ad hoc availability.
workflows.outcome: Reserved, governed engineering capacity with explicit service envelope, backlog, release rhythm, evidence and escalation path.
discovery: What response and release cadence matters?
Which changes are included versus separately scoped?
What after-hours coverage is truly required?
workflows.roi: Track availability, release lead time, backlog age, avoided emergency mobilization and continued workflow value against reserved capacity.

objections.q: Can we call only when something breaks?
objections.a: Ad hoc rescue remains available when capacity permits. A retainer reserves context, cadence and response so the system does not drift into emergency-only maintenance.

workflows.talkTrack: The retainer protects operational continuity and safe change. It is reserved engineering ownership, not an unlimited bucket of hours.

proofRules: Lead with buyer consequence and controlled outcome, not a technology list.
Label evidence as verified, directional, inferred or pending.
Use anonymized examples unless a client has approved public attribution.
Never claim professional authority CAD Guardian does not hold.
Never publish savings without a buyer-specific baseline.
Show native-file QA, exception handling, rollback and ownership as part of the product.
Treat recruiting opportunities as market intelligence; do not present them as client wins.
